name: <html>
description: The root element of an HTML document; every other element is nested inside it.
parameters: lang — declares the document's language for accessibility tools and search engines.

name: <head>
description: Container for machine-readable metadata about the document — title, character set, styles, scripts — that isn't rendered on the page itself.

name: <body>
description: Contains all the visible content of an HTML document — text, images, links and every other rendered element.
notes: A document can only have one <body>.

name: <title>
description: Sets the document's title, shown in the browser tab, bookmarks and search engine results.
notes: Must be placed inside <head>; each document should have exactly one <title>.

name: <meta>
description: Defines metadata such as character encoding, viewport settings, author or SEO description that isn't represented by other head elements.
parameters: charset — document encoding. name/content — key-value metadata pair. viewport — controls responsive scaling on mobile.
notes: A self-closing, void element — it has no closing tag or children.

name: <link>
description: Links an external resource — most commonly a CSS stylesheet, but also favicons, preloads and fonts — to the document.
parameters: rel — relationship to the document (e.g. stylesheet, icon, preload). href — URL of the resource.
notes: Void element; belongs in <head>.

name: <script>
description: Embeds or references JavaScript that runs in the page, either inline or via an external file.
parameters: src — path to an external script. defer — runs the script after HTML parsing. async — runs it as soon as it's downloaded, without blocking parsing.
notes: A script without defer/async blocks HTML parsing at the point it appears, which is why scripts are often placed before </body>.

name: <style>
description: Embeds CSS rules directly inside the document rather than linking an external stylesheet.
notes: Best used for small, page-specific styles; prefer <link> for shared stylesheets.

description: Represents a paragraph of text — a self-contained block of related content.

name: <h1>–<h6>
description: Six levels of section headings, <h1> being the most important and <h6> the least, used to structure a document's outline.
notes: Use heading levels in order for accessibility and SEO — don't skip levels purely for visual size (use CSS for that instead).

name: <a>
description: Creates a hyperlink to another page, a location within the page, a file or an email/phone address.
parameters: href — destination URL. target — where to open it (e.g. _blank). rel — relationship, such as noopener for security on external links.
notes: Use rel="noopener noreferrer" with target="_blank" to prevent the new page from accessing window.opener.

name: <span>
description: A generic inline container with no semantic meaning, used to style or script a piece of text.
notes: Prefer a semantic inline element (like <strong> or <time>) over <span> when one fits the meaning.

name: <div>
description: A generic block-level container with no semantic meaning, used for grouping elements for styling or scripting.
notes: Prefer a semantic element (<section>, <article>, <nav>, etc.) over <div> when the content has meaning.

description: Inserts a single line break within text, such as in an address or poem.
notes: Void element. Don't use it to add spacing between block elements — use CSS margin instead.

name: <hr>
description: Represents a thematic break between paragraphs or sections, typically rendered as a horizontal line.
notes: Void element.

name: <strong>
description: Marks text as having strong importance, seriousness or urgency; browsers render it bold by default.
notes: Semantic — conveys importance to screen readers, unlike <b> which is purely visual.

name: <em>
description: Marks text with stressed emphasis, typically changing the meaning of the sentence; browsers render it italic by default.
notes: Semantic emphasis, as opposed to <i> which is purely visual italics.

name: <b>
description: Draws visual attention to text (bold) without implying extra importance — a stylistic offset, not a semantic one.
notes: Use <strong> instead when the text is actually important, not just visually bold.

name: <i>
description: Represents text in an alternate voice or mood, such as a technical term, foreign phrase or ship name — rendered italic.
notes: Use <em> instead when the text carries actual emphasis rather than just an alternate tone.

name: <sub>
description: Renders text as subscript, lower and smaller than the surrounding text — commonly used in chemical formulas or footnotes.

name: <sup>
description: Renders text as superscript, raised and smaller than the surrounding text — commonly used for exponents or ordinal suffixes.

name: <abbr>
description: Marks up an abbreviation or acronym, optionally providing its full expansion via the title attribute.
parameters: title — the full expansion, shown as a tooltip on hover.

name: <q>
description: Marks a short, inline quotation; browsers typically wrap the content in quotation marks automatically.
parameters: cite — optional URL of the quote's source.
notes: Use <blockquote> instead for longer, block-level quotations.

name: <blockquote>
description: Represents an extended quotation set off from the surrounding text as its own block.
parameters: cite — optional URL identifying the source of the quotation.
example: The best code is no code at all.

name: <pre>
description: Preserves whitespace and line breaks exactly as written, rendering the content in a monospace font.
example:
function add(a, b) {
  return a + b;
}
notes: Commonly wraps a <code> element for displaying code blocks.

name: <code>
description: Marks up a short fragment of computer code, rendered in a monospace font.
notes: Wrap in <pre> to preserve formatting for multi-line code blocks.

name: <ul>
description: Groups a set of items into an unordered (bulleted) list.

name: <ol>
description: Groups a set of items into an ordered (numbered) list.
parameters: start — the number to begin counting from. reversed — counts down instead of up.

name: <li>
description: Represents a single item within a <ul>, <ol> or <menu> list.
parameters: value — overrides the item's number, only meaningful inside an <ol>.

name: <dl>
description: A description list that pairs terms with their descriptions, such as a glossary or metadata list.

name: <dt>
description: Defines a term or name inside a <dl> description list.
notes: Must be followed by one or more <dd> elements.

name: <dd>
description: Provides the description or value for the preceding <dt> term inside a <dl> list.

name: <table>
description: Represents tabular data organized into rows and columns.
notes: Use tables for actual tabular data, not for page layout.

name: <thead>
description: Groups the header row(s) of a table, separating column labels from the body data.

name: <tbody>
description: Groups the main body rows of a table, distinct from its header and footer.

name: <tr>
description: Represents a single row of cells within a table.

name: <th>
description: Defines a header cell in a table, labeling a row or column; rendered bold and centered by default.
parameters: scope — indicates whether the header applies to a row or column, improving screen-reader table navigation.

name: <td>
description: Defines a standard data cell within a table row.
parameters: colspan — number of columns to span. rowspan — number of rows to span.

name: <caption>
description: Provides a title or explanation for a table, announced by screen readers before the table content.
notes: Must be the first child of <table>.

description: Embeds an image into the document.
parameters: src — image URL. alt — alternative text for accessibility and when the image fails to load. width/height — intrinsic dimensions to avoid layout shift.
notes: Void element. Always provide alt text (empty alt="" for purely decorative images).

name: <video>
description: Embeds a video player, optionally with playback controls and multiple source fallbacks.
parameters: controls — shows the native player UI. autoplay, loop, muted — playback behavior. poster — preview image before playback.
notes: Browsers block autoplay with sound unless muted is also set.

name: <audio>
description: Embeds an audio player for playing sound or music files.
parameters: controls — shows native playback controls. autoplay, loop, muted — playback behavior.

name: <source>
description: Specifies an alternate media resource for <video>, <audio> or <picture>, letting the browser pick the best supported format.
parameters: src/srcset — resource URL. type — MIME type. media — condition for <picture> sources.
notes: Void element; the browser uses the first <source> it supports.

name: <picture>
description: Wraps multiple candidates and a fallback , letting the browser choose the best image for the screen size or format.
notes: Used for art direction and serving next-gen image formats with fallbacks.

name: <track>
description: Adds timed text tracks — subtitles, captions or descriptions — to a <video> or <audio> element.
parameters: kind — subtitles, captions, descriptions, chapters. src — WebVTT file URL. srclang — language code.
example:
<video controls>
  <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
  <track src="en.vtt" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" label="English" />
</video>
notes: Void element; important for accessibility.

name: <iframe>
description: Embeds another HTML document (a map, video, ad, or entire site) as a nested browsing context within the current page.
parameters: src — URL to embed. title — accessible name for the frame. loading — 'lazy' to defer offscreen loading.
notes: Always set a title attribute for screen-reader users, and use sandbox for untrusted content.

name: <canvas>
description: Provides a blank, scriptable bitmap surface for drawing graphics, charts or animations via JavaScript.
parameters: width/height — drawing surface dimensions in pixels.
notes: The element itself is just a container — drawing requires the Canvas 2D or WebGL API via JavaScript.

name: <svg>
description: Embeds Scalable Vector Graphics directly in HTML, defining shapes and paths that stay crisp at any resolution.
parameters: viewBox — coordinate system of the drawing. width/height — rendered size.
notes: Unlike <canvas>, SVG content is part of the DOM and can be styled with CSS.

name: <template>
description: Holds HTML markup that is parsed but not rendered or executed until it is cloned into the document via JavaScript.
notes: Commonly used with Web Components and client-side rendering of repeated markup.

name: <dialog>
description: Represents a native modal or non-modal dialog box, such as a confirmation prompt or an interactive popup.
parameters: open — shows the dialog non-modally. showModal()/close() — JS methods to control modal display.
notes: showModal() traps focus and adds a ::backdrop, unlike setting the open attribute directly.
